# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).

type PersonFields = { name?: string; grade?: string; gradeFrom?: string; terms?: string; termsFrom?: string; contact?: string; tags?: string };

/** Fill the person form. `clear` (an add) also empties every optional field the test does not
 *  give, so nothing typed for a refused add carries into this one; an edit leaves the
 *  fields it is not given as the editor filled them. */
async function fillPersonForm(page: Page, f: PersonFields, clear = false) {
  if (f.name !== undefined) await page.getByTestId('person-form-name').fill(f.name);
  if (f.grade !== undefined) await page.getByTestId('person-form-grade').selectOption(f.grade);
  for (const [key, testid] of [['gradeFrom', 'person-form-grade-from'], ['terms', 'person-form-terms'],
    ['termsFrom', 'person-form-terms-from'], ['contact', 'person-form-contact'], ['tags', 'person-form-tags']] as const) {
    const v = f[key];
    if (v !== undefined) await page.getByTestId(testid).fill(v);
    else if (clear) await setField(page, testid, undefined);
  }
}

/** Add a person through the form. The new row's id, or null when the form refused. */
export async function addPerson(page: Page, f: PersonFields & { name: string; grade: string }): Promise<string | null> {
  const before = await ids(rows(page), 'person-row-');
  await fillPersonForm(page, f, true);
  await page.getByTestId('person-form-submit').click();
  let added: string | null = null;
  const ok = await until(page, async () => (added = await addedPerson(page, before, f.name)) !== null,
    page.getByTestId('person-form-error'), 'add person');
  return ok ? added : null;
}

export async function editOpen(page: Page, personId: string): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByTestId(`person-edit-${personId}`).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('person-form-name')).not.toHaveValue('', { timeout: WAIT });
  editing.set(page, personId);
}

/**
 * Save the open editor with these changes; true when saved, false when the form refused. `shows` is
 * the grade the row shows once saved: by default the grade entered, but a grade dated from another
 * day may leave the grade in force on the sheet's today unchanged.
 */
type Shows = string | { grade?: string; terms?: string };

export async function editSave(page: Page, f: PersonFields, shows?: Shows): Promise<boolean> {
  const id = editing.get(page);
  if (!id) throw new Error('editSave without editOpen');
  const want = typeof shows === 'string' ? { grade: shows } : (shows ?? {});
  const grade = want.grade ?? f.grade;                       // the grade the row shows once saved
  const terms = want.terms ?? f.terms;                       // the terms in force the row shows
  const r = row(page, id);
  const shows_ = async () => {
    if (f.name !== undefined && plainName(await shown(r.getByTestId('person-name'))) !== f.name.trim()) return false;
    if (grade !== undefined && await shown(r.getByTestId('person-grade')) !== grade) return false;
    if (terms !== undefined && await shown(r.getByTestId('person-terms')) !== terms) return false;
    return !(await page.getByTestId('person-form-error').isVisible().catch(() => false));
  };
  // a save the row cannot show (the values it checks are already there) is judged by its error
  const already = await shows_();
  await fillPersonForm(page, f);
  await page.getByTestId('person-form-submit').click();
  return until(page, shows_, page.getByTestId('person-form-error'), 'save person', already);
}

export async function editPerson(page: Page, personId: string, f: PersonFields, shows?: Shows): Promise<boolean> {
  await editOpen(page, personId);
  return editSave(page, f, shows);
}

  const terms = want.terms ?? f.terms;                       // the terms in force the row shows
  const r = row(page, id);
  const shows_ = async () => {
    if (f.name !== undefined && plainName(await shown(r.getByTestId('person-name'))) !== f.name.trim()) return false;
    if (grade !== undefined && await shown(r.getByTestId('person-grade')) !== grade) return false;
    if (terms !== undefined && await shown(r.getByTestId('person-terms')) !== terms) return false;
    return !(await page.getByTestId('person-form-error').isVisible().catch(() => false));
  };
  // a save the row cannot show (the values it checks are already there) is judged by its error
  const already = await shows_();
  await fillPersonForm(page, f);
  await page.getByTestId('person-form-submit').click();
  return until(page, shows_, page.getByTestId('person-form-error'), 'save person', already);
}

export async function editPerson(page: Page, personId: string, f: PersonFields, shows?: Shows): Promise<boolean> {
  await editOpen(page, personId);
  return editSave(page, f, shows);
}

-- The sheet's terms: a claim is due by its date plus this many days.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN terms INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 14;
-- Terms set for a grade: a claim whose person has that grade on its date is due by its date plus them. A grade
-- without its own terms uses the sheet's terms.
CREATE TABLE grade_terms (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    grade VARCHAR(1) NOT NULL,
    terms INT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, grade)
);
-- A claim's due-by, fixed when it is created: its date plus the terms of its person's grade in force on its date.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN due_by DATE;
UPDATE claim SET due_by = DATEADD(DAY, (SELECT s.terms FROM sheet s WHERE s.id = claim.sheet_id), claim_date);
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN due_by SET NOT NULL;
-- A dated setting's values, each in force from its date until the next one's; before every from-date the
-- sheet's starting value (floor 1.00, late percent 0.00, terms 14; none for the clerk limit, the cap and a
-- grade's own terms). setting_value null: blank (no limit, no cap, a grade without its own terms).
CREATE TABLE setting_from (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    setting_key VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE NOT NULL,
    setting_value VARCHAR(30),
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date)
);
-- Values already set carry over as in force from the start.
INSERT INTO setting_from (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT id, 'floor', DATE '1900-01-01', CAST(due_floor AS VARCHAR(30)) FROM sheet WHERE due_floor <> 1.00;
INSERT INTO setting_from (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT id, 'late-pct', DATE '1900-01-01', CAST(late_pct AS VARCHAR(30)) FROM sheet WHERE late_pct <> 0.00;
INSERT INTO setting_from (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT id, 'terms', DATE '1900-01-01', CAST(terms AS VARCHAR(30)) FROM sheet WHERE terms <> 14;
INSERT INTO setting_from (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)

INSERT INTO setting_from (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT id, 'cap', DATE '1900-01-01', CAST(due_cap AS VARCHAR(30)) FROM sheet WHERE due_cap IS NOT NULL;
INSERT INTO setting_from (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting_value)
    SELECT sheet_id, 'terms-' || grade, DATE '1900-01-01', CAST(terms AS VARCHAR(30)) FROM grade_terms;

-- the person was given). The grade in force on a date is the one with the latest from-date on or before

CREATE TABLE person_grade (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    grade VARCHAR(1) NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE
);
CREATE INDEX person_grade_sheet ON person_grade (sheet_id, person_id);

-- The sheet's terms: a claim is due by its date plus this many days.

-- Terms set for a grade: a claim whose person has that grade on its date is due by its date plus them. A grade
-- without its own terms uses the sheet's terms.
CREATE TABLE grade_terms (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    grade VARCHAR(1) NOT NULL,
    terms INT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, grade)
);
-- A claim's due-by, fixed when it is created: its date plus the terms of its person's grade in force on its date.

    setting_value VARCHAR(30),

);

A person can now have their own terms, and all 4 tests in the spec pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What works now:**
- **Person form:** a new terms field (`person-form-terms`). Blank means the person has no terms of their own. Any value that isn't a whole number of days, 0 or more, is refused with the form's error, and nothing is stored or audited.
- **Row:** the person's terms show in a new Terms column (`person-terms`), empty when they have none.
- **Due-by:** fixed when the claim is created, using the first of: the person's own terms, their grade's terms, then the sheet's terms. The grade and sheet terms are the ones in force on the claim's date. This applies to claims added from a row, pasted claims and claims split off another.
- **Audit:**
  - `PERSON_ADDED` ends with `terms=<days>` only when the form gave a value.
  - `PERSON_EDITED` ends with `terms=<days>` only when the terms changed from what the person had before the save, or with `terms=` when they were cleared. An edit that leaves them unchanged adds nothing.

**Two things to know:**
- **Refused edits now close the editor.** When a person edit is refused (any refusal except the "someone else saved this person meanwhile" conflict), the form goes back to adding and keeps the error showing. Before, it stayed open on that person. I changed this because the test types the next new person into the same form right after a refused edit. Without the change, that add would have been sent as an edit and renamed the person being edited instead of adding a new one.
- **A person's own terms are not dated.** The claim uses whatever terms the person has when the claim is created, whatever the claim's date. The spec never fills the terms from-date field (`person-form-terms-from`) that the test helpers know about, so I didn't add one.

The stored data change is a new migration, `V43__person_terms.sql`, which adds a nullable `terms` column to `person`. On the server, the main changes are in `Person`, `PersonRequest`/`ValidatePersonRequest`, `ApplyPerson`, the two audit classes, `PersonRepository` and `BuildClaim`, plus a new `PersonTermsChange` record. On the front end, the changes are in `people.ts`, `PersonForm.tsx` and `PeopleList.tsx`.
